title: Gluing | Clo 2026.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new gluing feature in CLO 2026.0 allows you to attach patterns to desired locations using various methods such as fill, brush, or sticker. Simulate accessory patterns like pockets or labels to naturally follow the garment's movements. Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

markdown_content: ## Gluing in CLO 2026.0 (Sticker, Glue Brush, Glue Fill) This section introduces the three new gluing tools in **CLO 2026.0**—**Sticker**, **Glue Brush**, and **Glue Fill**—and where to find them in the **2D toolbar**. It also clarifies which tools can be used in **2D vs 3D**. In **CLO 2026.0**, the gluing features are located in the **2D toolbar** and include three tools: 1. **Sticker** 2. **Glue Brush** 3. **Glue Fill** These tools allow you to create glue relationships between pattern pieces so that, after **Simulate**, the glued parts move/attach as intended. --- ## Sticker Tool (2D-only) — Ghost Shape + Glue Placement This section explains how the **Sticker** tool works in **2D**: creating a **ghost shape**, placing it onto a target pattern, and understanding how glue info behaves after you switch tools. Key behavior: - The **Sticker** tool can **only be used in the 2D window**. - You **cannot apply** the sticker in the **3D** window. Workflow: 1. Go to the **2D** window. 2. Click once on the shape/pattern piece you want to glue. 3. A **ghost shape** appears. 4. Place the ghost shape onto the pattern you want it glued to. 5. CLO shows an **arrow** indicating which pattern is being glued to which, and the ghost’s shape. After setup: - Run **Simulate** to confirm it attaches correctly. - If you click away and switch to **Transform Pattern**, the visible glue info disappears and the editing space looks normal. If you want to see glue placement again: - Select the glued shape → **right-click** → **Clone as internal shape**. - Place it and add the **sticker** again if needed. Important limitation / warning: - If you try to glue onto a pattern that is **already glued**, CLO shows a popup: **“The pattern is already glued, please remove the existing.”** - To remove existing gluing, you must use a **different glue tool** (not Sticker again). --- ## Removing Sticker Gluing (Use Glue Fill or Glue Brush Subtract) This section covers how to remove existing gluing when Sticker reports that the pattern is already glued, using **Glue Fill** or **Glue Brush** with **subtract/minus**. Removal approach: - Use either **Fill Glue** or **Brush Glue** to remove glue relationships. Example using **Fill Glue**: 1. Select **Fill Glue**. 2. A popup appears with options to **add or subtract**. 3. Choose **subtract**. 4. Use **minus** on the area/pattern that is currently glued. 5. The glued portion is erased. 6. Return to **Sticker** and place the internal shape again on top. 7. **Simulate** to verify the new glue placement. --- ## Glue Brush Tool — Add/Subtract, Size, and Over vs Under This section explains the **Glue Brush** tool options (add/subtract, brush size, and **over vs under**), including contact requirements in **3D** and when to use **over** for “top of” gluing vs **under** for trims. Glue Brush options: - **Over / Under**: determines whether you glue as “over” (on top) or “under” (beneath) - **Mode**: **add** or **subtract** - **Size**: brush thickness/extent ### Over mode (pattern-to-pattern “on top” gluing) - Use **Over** when one pattern piece should glue **over** another (e.g., “over to over” relationships). - Set **Mode** to **add**. - Choose an appropriate **Size**. Brush usage: 1. Click once, then **click and hold** to draw a glue line. 2. If you release and see **“no contact detected”**, it means the pattern piece is too far apart in **3D space** for CLO to detect contact. Fix for “no contact detected” in 3D: - Go to **Select Move**. - Reposition the piece so it touches the target. - Then return to the **brush** and apply again. ### Under mode (trims) - Use **Under** for **trims**—gluing trims to patterns from beneath. - Set **Under**, then apply glue onto the trim/pattern boundary. - Use **Simulate** to confirm attachment. ### 2D and 3D capability - The **Glue Brush** can be used in **both 2D and 3D**. - However, in **3D**, it may fail if there is no detected contact (pieces are not touching). ### Subtract capability - The brush can also **subtract** glue (remove relationships) when needed. --- ## Glue Fill Tool — Contact-based Fill, Multi-piece Overlaps This section explains **Fill Glue** behavior: applying glue via **add** in **2D or 3D**, requiring **contact**, and supporting filling across **overlapping multiple pattern pieces**. Key behavior: - **Fill Glue** can be used in **both 2D and 3D**. - You must ensure **contact** between pieces for CLO to recognize the glue area. - You can fill glue across **multiple pattern pieces at once**. Workflow in 2D: 1. In the **2D** window, click a region/pattern piece. 2. Choose **add**. 3. CLO applies the glue fill. Workflow in 3D: 1. In the **3D** window, click **add**. 2. Place it so it sits **directly on top** of the target with contact. 3. Contact detection enables the fill. Overlapping pieces: - If a pattern overlaps two different pattern pieces, you can apply **add** and CLO will detect the overlap across both. - After **Simulate**, the glue behavior reflects those multiple attachments. --- ## Practice: Gluing a Garment (2D for Precision with Folds; Then Simulate) This section demonstrates a practical garment gluing workflow using **Sticker**, **Glue Brush**, and **Glue Fill**, with guidance on how to handle folds and placement precision. Garment workflow highlights: - When the garment has **many folds**, gluing in **3D** may be less precise. - Prefer **2D** for precision placement. Example sequence: 1. Use **Sticker** to attach a gluing element in **2D** at a specific location. 2. Switch to the **Glue Brush** in **2D** to glue along the folded/glued areas (“glue right on top”). 3. For additional glue regions, use **Fill/Bucket-style fill** (referred to as a bucket in the demo): - Select the relevant pattern/region. - Place it at the desired location. - Apply **add**. 4. Run **Simulate** to confirm all glued elements behave correctly. --- ## Practice: Gluing Shoes (Inside-out Layering Strategy) This section covers gluing for **shoes**, including placement in 2D vs 3D and a recommended ordering strategy: **work from the inside out** (bottom layers first). Shoe workflow: - You can glue in **3D** by placing pieces in position, then using **glue bucket/add**, but the demo uses **2D** for faster, exact placement. - In **2D**, place parts directly where you want them, then apply glue. Layering guidance (important): - **Best practice:** work **from the inside out**. - Start with the **bottom layer** and move forward to higher/top layers. - Avoid gluing **top layers first**. If placement needs adjustment: - When something “happens” or alignment needs improvement, you can **scooch/scoot** the piece out, then **Simulate** again to get easier/better placement. Glue visualization: - When multiple pattern pieces overlap or one sits on top of others, CLO shows **arrows** indicating attachments. - The system may “reset itself” during the process, but the demo indicates it sorts out attachments after simulation. --- ## Using Brush After Unfreezing (Add More Gluing on Top) This section describes an additional workflow where the user **unfreezes** and then applies the **Glue Brush** again to add more glue on top of existing setups. Additional steps shown: 1. **Unfreeze** the current state (so edits can be applied again). 2. Use the **Glue Brush** tool. 3. Apply additional **add** gluing on the targeted area. 4. Run **Simulate**. 5. Use brush strokes to achieve a **nice, straight** glue placement. 6. Confirm the resulting glue relationships across the relevant pattern pieces.
